question.value: Study the effects of recent massive star formation in the starburst pseudo-ring and AGN activity in the circumnuclear disc of NGC 1068 on the vibrational excitation of HC3N and heating of gas and dust.

evidence.quote: NGC 1068, one of the closest galaxies hosting spatially resolved AGN and starburst (SB) activities, offers a unique opportunity to study the effects of star formation and AGN activity from its ~10^7 M_\odot SMBH (cite: Davis2014; Combes2019) on the vibrational excitation of HC$_3$N.
In this paper we study the HC$_3$N emission in the CND and the SB pseudo-ring of NGC 1068.
Fortunately, project-ID 2011.0.00083.S (cite: SGB2014) is an eleven-field mosaic that fully covers the SB pseudo-ring.

findings_qualitative.value: Vibrationally excited HC3N (v7=1) is detected only towards one star-forming clump (the SHC) in the northern SB pseudo-ring and is not detected in the CND despite its high v=0 HC3N column density.

evidence.quote: We have detected emission from vibrationally excited HC$_3$N (HC$_3$N\*) only towards one star-forming region of the SB ring. Remarkably, HC$_3$N\* was not detected towards the CND despite its large HC$_3$N $v=0$ column density.

findings_qualitative.value: The SHC has high dust temperature (~250 K), high density (~6e5 cm^-3), and IR luminosity (~5.8e8 L_sun) typical of internally heated proto-Super Star Clusters (proto-SSCs).

evidence.quote: From LTE and non-LTE modelling of HC$_3$N\*, we obtained a dust temperature of $T_\text{dust} \sim 250$ K and a density of $n_{\text{H}_2}=6\times10^5$ cm$^{-3}$ for this star-forming region. The estimated IR luminosity of $5.8\times10^8$ L$_\odot$ is typical of proto-Super Star Clusters (proto-SSC) observed in the SB galaxy NGC 253.

findings_qualitative.value: The dust in the CND has a low temperature (<= 100 K) because it is heated externally by the AGN in an open geometry where IR photon trapping is negligible, whereas the SHC is heated internally in an IR optically thick closed geometry with strong back-warming.

evidence.loc: On the heating of the SHC and the CND
evidence.quote: This indicates that the dust in the CND not being efficiently heated by the AGN is due to being externally irradiated by the AGN (i.e. geometrical open system), where photon trapping in the IR is negligible and the temperature profile follows effectively the optically thin case.

findings_qualitative.value: The young SSCs in the SB pseudo-ring are concentrated near the contact points connecting the nuclear bar with the spiral arms, supporting gas inflow, and show no systematic age gradient along the ring, supporting the 'popcorn' star formation scenario.

evidence.quote: The SSCs location and derived young ages are closely associated to the region connecting the nuclear bar with the SB pseudo-ring, where most of the gas is being accumulated and an increase of cloud-cloud collisions is expected.
We do not find any systematic trend of the ages of the SSCs within the ring, supporting the “popcorn” mode of star formation.

findings_qualitative.value: Detection of HC3N* alone cannot discriminate between AGN and starburst heating in heavily obscured galactic nuclei (closed systems) like NGC 4418 and Arp 220 without spatially resolving the T_vib profile.

evidence.quote: We concluded that just the detection of HC$_3$N\* emission cannot be used as a discriminator because of the greenhouse effect in heavily obscured galactic nuclei (closed systems) makes the AGN and SB dust profiles to be similar at large distances.

claims.hypothesis: Vibrationally excited HC3N (HC3N*) traces embedded early massive star formation (Super Hot Cores / proto-SSCs) heated internally by massive protostars.
claims.experiment: Search for HC3N v=0 and v7=1 transitions across the SB pseudo-ring of NGC 1068 and perform LTE and non-LTE radiative transfer modelling of the detected emission.
claims.result: HC3N* (v7=1, J=16-15 and 24-23) is detected in one clump (SHC) with T_vib = 236 +/- 18 K, T_d = 248 +/- 28 K, n_H2 = 5.9e5 cm^-3, and L_IR = 5.8e8 L_sun.
claims.finding: The clump is a Super Hot Core tracing the proto-SSC phase (~6e4 yr old), internally heated by massive protostars in an IR optically thick environment.

evidence.quote: This is consistent with the derived $T_\text{dust}$ and H$_2$ densities from our non-LTE analysis of $248\pm28$ K and $(5.9\pm0.2)\times10 ^5$ cm$^{-3}$, respectively. The latter indicates that we are observing a Super Hot Core (SHC) similar to those observed in NGC 253 (cite: Rico2020).

From the dust temperature and the lower limit to the size of the SHC in the SB pseudo-ring we estimated an IR luminosity of $\sim5.8\times10^8$ L$_\odot$, typical of the proto-Stellar Star Clusters (proto-SSC) observed in NGC 253

claims.hypothesis: The luminous AGN in NGC 1068 efficiently heats the dust in the surrounding circumnuclear disc (CND) to excite HC3N* emission.
claims.experiment: Measure HC3N v=0 and v7=1 lines towards CND East and West and derive excitation temperatures, dust temperatures, and densities using LTE and non-LTE models.
claims.result: HC3N* is not detected in the CND despite log N(HC3N) ~ 15.0-16.0 cm^-2; upper limits are T_vib <= 98 K (CND E) and <= 117 K (CND W), and T_d <= 75 K (CND E).
claims.finding: The AGN is inefficient at heating the CND dust radiatively because the CND is heated externally in an open system, reaching only ~57 K as predicted by the optically thin Stefan-Boltzmann law.

evidence.quote: We show that, contrary to massive proto-stars, the AGN is extremely efficient in heating the gas of the CND mainly through shocks originating in the jet/outflow system, but very inefficient in heating the dust by radiation, which is the requirement for HC$_3$N to be vibrationally excited for the derived H$_2$ densities.

The low dust temperature $<100$ K derived towards the CND, is consistent with the expected heating by the AGN in NGC 1068 for a luminosity of $1.1\times10^{11}$ L$_\odot$ considering the IR optically thin case and that the dust in the CND is being externally heated (open system).

claims.hypothesis: Star formation in the SB pseudo-ring is triggered at the bar-arm contact points and propagates sequentially along the ring ('pearls on a string' vs 'popcorn' scenario).
claims.experiment: Derive stellar masses and ages of 15 SSCs and 2 Pa alpha sources using 147 GHz continuum, 350 GHz continuum, Pa alpha, and HC3N*, and compare ages with angular separation from the nuclear bar.
claims.result: Most young SSCs (ages 6e4 to 4e5 yr) are located near the NE and SW contact points of the nuclear bar and spiral arms (PA = 46 deg), with no systematic age gradient along the ring.
claims.finding: The spatial concentration supports the bar-driven gas inflow scenario, while the lack of an ordered age sequence along the ring supports the 'popcorn' scenario over 'pearls on a string'.

evidence.loc: Propagation of SSC formation in the ring
evidence.quote: However, if we consider the different SSCs ages (from Table [\[tab:summary_masses\]](#tab:summary_masses)) ant their projected location relative to the nuclear bar (Figure 6), it seems that there is no ordered sequence of the star forming regions inside these two regions. This would be in accordance with the “popcorn” scenario instead of the “pearls on a string” scenario described by (cite: Boker2008).

The SSCs location and derived young ages are closely associated to the region connecting the nuclear bar with the SB pseudo-ring, where most of the gas is being accumulated and an increase of cloud-cloud collisions is expected.

claims.hypothesis: HC3N* emission alone can discriminate between AGN and starburst heating in heavily obscured galactic nuclei such as NGC 4418 and Arp 220.
claims.experiment: Compare the HC3N* emitting region sizes of NGC 4418 and Arp 220 with predictions from optically thin external AGN heating and optically thick closed-system models with back-warming.
claims.result: Optically thin AGN heating predicts tiny sizes (2.5 and 8.0 pc) compared to observed lower limits (12 and 80 pc), but optically thick closed-system models with back-warming predict T_d > 300 K sizes of ~20 pc and ~100 pc regardless of whether the central source is an AGN or SB.
claims.finding: Simply detecting HC3N* cannot discriminate between AGN and SB activity in closed optically thick nuclei; high spatial resolution mapping of the T_vib gradient is required.

evidence.loc: HC$_3$N\* as a discriminator between AGN and star formation activity in galaxies
evidence.quote: Therefore, discriminating between AGN and SB heating using HC$_3$N\* emission in IR optically thick galaxy nuclei can only be done when the spatial resolution is high enough to measure the $T_\text{vib}$ profile close to the central heating source, where the temperature gradient is expected to show the largest difference between the AGN and SB heating.

why_this_data.value: NGC 1068 is one of the closest galaxies with spatially resolved AGN and starburst activities and enhanced HC3N abundance in the CND; ALMA archive provides multi-frequency coverage including an 11-field mosaic covering the SB pseudo-ring.

evidence.quote: NGC 1068, one of the closest galaxies hosting spatially resolved AGN and starburst (SB) activities, offers a unique opportunity to study the effects of star formation and AGN activity from its $\sim10^7$ M$_\odot$ SMBH (cite: Davis2014; Combes2019) on the vibrational excitation of HC$_3$N.
Fortunately, project-ID 2011.0.00083.S (cite: SGB2014) is an eleven-field mosaic that fully covers the SB pseudo-ring.

why_this_method.value: Data were not continuum subtracted in the uv-plane due to abundant molecular emission and large velocity gradients; MADCUBA SLIM and non-LTE radiative transfer modelling account for line profiles, opacity, blending, and different excitation mechanisms (IR pumping vs collisions).

evidence.quote: Due to the large amount of molecular emission and the large velocity gradients between the CND and the SB pseudo-ring data were not continuum subtracted in the uv-plane.
To fully account for the line profiles, opacity effects and line blending we have also carried out an LTE analysis of the HC$_3$N\* emission using MADCUBA SLIM tool (cite: Madcuba2019).

To derive the physical properties of the SHC and the CND and to properly account for the different excitation mechanisms of the vibrational and rotational HC$_3$N transitions, we have carried out a non-LTE radiative transfer modelling

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Low dust optical depth at 45 um as the cause for inefficient IR pumping of HC3N* in the CND (rejected because N(H2) ~ 10^24 cm^-2 gives tau_45um ~ 16).

evidence.loc: On the heating of the SHC and the CND
evidence.quote: The first possibility can be ruled out since the H$_2$ column densities in the CND are $\sim10^{24}$ cm$^{-2}$ (see Table [\[tab:table_hc3n_lums\]](#tab:table_hc3n_lums)), which translates to dust opacities at $45$ $\mu$m of $\tau \sim16$.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Collisional excitation of HC3N vibrational levels (rejected because derived H2 densities are much lower than the critical density for vibrational levels).

evidence.loc: On the heating of the SHC and the CND
evidence.quote: The derived H$_2$ densities for both the SHC and the CND positions are similar, but much lower than the critical density for collisional excitation of the vibrational levels (cite: Wyrowski1999).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: 'Pearls on a string' scenario for sequential star formation along the SB pseudo-ring (rejected in favor of the 'popcorn' scenario due to lack of ordered age sequence).

evidence.loc: Propagation of SSC formation in the ring
evidence.quote: This would be in accordance with the “popcorn” scenario instead of the “pearls on a string” scenario described by (cite: Boker2008).

limitations_admitted.value: Decreased sensitivity at the edges of single-pointing maps at ~220 GHz where the SB pseudo-ring is located.

evidence.quote: Since most of the NGC 1068 observations are centered on the AGN position, as we move to higher frequencies the observed field of view of the telescope primary beam is reduced, limiting the observations of the SB pseudo-ring to the outer edge of the mapped area at $\sim220$ GHz. As a consequence there is a decrease in sensitivity at the edges of the map where the SB pseudo-ring is observed.

limitations_admitted.value: Lack of sensitivity prevents detecting HC3N* in other SSCs or ruling out the presence of proto-SSCs in SSC 7 and 8.

evidence.quote: The lack of sensitivity prevented us from detecting HC$_3$N\* emission towards any other position in the SB pseudo-ring.
From the non-detection of HC$_3$N\* in other star-forming regions of the SB pseudo-ring we cannot completely rule out the presence of SHCs

limitations_admitted.value: Strong line blending of HC3N J=38-37 with CO(3-2) and J=39-38 with HCN(4-3) in the CND due to broad line FWHMs.

evidence.quote: ^a^ Strongly blended with CO(3-2) due to the higher FWHMs in the CND (see Table [\[tab:table_hc3n_lums\]](#tab:table_hc3n_lums)).
^b^ Blended with HCN(4-3) due to the higher FWHMs in the CND (see Table [\[tab:table_hc3n_lums\]](#tab:table_hc3n_lums)).

limitations_admitted.value: Different beam sizes between VLA 8.4 GHz and ALMA 147 GHz continuum observations; 2x uncertainty in gas masses from assumed T_dust = 80 K.

evidence.quote: However, the beam sizes are rather different.

evidence.loc: Stellar and gas masses in the SB pseudo-ring
evidence.quote: Changes in a factor of $2$ in $T_\text{dust}$ will change the masses by a similar factor.

referee_caveats_inferred: The multi-transition HC3N analysis combines ALMA datasets with synthesized beams ranging from 0.22''x0.19'' to 1.15''x0.99'', yet the text does not specify whether the cubes were convolved to a matched resolution prior to spectral extraction or how beam dilution across bands was handled.
Units for the integrated HC3N line fluxes in Table 5 are omitted from the table header and caption (likely Jy km s^-1 or mJy km s^-1 or K km s^-1).
The SSC age calibration (Eq. 11) relies on a single ad-hoc scaling factor (13) anchored to the SHC and assumes a linear gas removal rate over 10 Myr, which is highly simplified.

methods_papers.why: Defines the LTE and non-LTE HC3N* analysis methodology, back-warming luminosity correction, and proto-SSC mass and age equations used throughout this paper.
Describes the non-LTE radiative transfer code and greenhouse/back-warming dust temperature profile models.
Provides the prescriptions for converting ionizing photon rates to ZAMS stellar masses and 350 GHz dust continuum to gas masses.
Provides the rotational diagram formalism and Einstein coefficient equations used for LTE analysis.
Describes the MADCUBA software and SLIM LTE line-fitting tool.
